deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Gauss is investigating the graduation (division) errors of the Repsold circle. psi(x) is the correction for division x. He defines f(x) = psi(x) - (1/4)[psi(x)+psi(x+90)+psi(x+180)+psi(x+270)], the part of the division error that is not periodic with period 90 deg (he expects the period-90 part to be negligible). The circle is set so that the lower microscope reads x, x+90, x+180, x+270 in turn. The left microscope (near 270 deg) gives seconds-readings a,b,c,d and the right microscope (near 90 deg) gives A,B,C,D. The model is a = lam + f0 - f3, b = lam + f1 - f0, ... and A = mu + f0 - f1, B = mu + f1 - f2, ..., with f0+f1+f2+f3 = 0. From these 8 equations Gauss took the least-squares values f(x) = (d+a-2b+A+B-2D)/8 and the three cyclic analogues. (Check, mine: substituting the model gives d+a-2b = 3f0-2f1-f2 and A+B-2D = 3f0-f2-2f3, which sum to 8f0.)

This page, step 1 (data of 20 April): for x = 15, 45, ..., 345 (every 30 deg) the left-microscope reading 270 deg 3'(a)'' and the right-microscope reading 90 deg 0'(b)'' are tabulated. This gives three independent 4-cycles: x ≡ 15, 45 and 75 (mod 90).

Step 2 ('Hieraus Abstand des Mikroskopes'): the mean seconds-reading of each microscope over each 4-cycle.
- Left microscope: 35.4500 (15,105,195,285), 34.4625 (45,...) and 34.7375 (75,...). The grand mean is 34.883, so the left microscope is at 270 deg 3'34.883''.
- Right microscope: 39.200, 38.650 and 38.925, grand mean 38.925, so it is at 90 deg 0'38.925''.
- These cycle means are the least-squares estimates of lam and mu, since f sums to zero over a cycle.

Step 3: f(x) is computed for all 12 x from the 1/8-formulas, cycle by cycle. Example, x = 15, using a = 34.00, b = 38.20, c = 36.30, d = 33.30, A = 37.95, B = 41.00, C = 40.30, D = 37.55:
f(15) = (33.30+34.00-76.40+37.95+41.00-75.10)/8 = -0.656.
The tabulated f values are -0.66, -0.25, +0.36, +0.62, +0.61, +1.00, +0.47, -0.02, +0.06, -0.44, -0.32, -1.43. Each 4-cycle sums to about 0.

Step 4: the first harmonic is fitted to the 12 values of f. For 12 equidistant points, least squares gives:
- alpha = (1/6) * sum f(x) cos x ≈ -0.747
- beta = (1/6) * sum f(x) sin x ≈ 0.355-0.358
Gauss writes f(x) ≈ -0.75'' cos x + 0.36'' sin x. That is a periodic division error of amplitude about 0.83'' with a phase near 154 deg.

Step 5: the formula is evaluated at the 12 points and the differences (formula minus f) are tabulated.

Step 6: 'Mittlerer Ablesungsfehler' (mean error of one microscope reading) = sqrt(0.68625) = 0.828''.
- The residuals used appear on the next page: 12 rows (lower-microscope settings) by 3 columns (lower, left, right microscope reading errors). Each row sums to zero.
- I verified row 1 myself, using the global lam = 34.883, mu = 38.925 and the sinusoidal f. The equation residuals are r_a = 0.794 and r_A = -0.198.
- Distributing them by least squares over the three readings (e0 = -(r_a+r_A)/3, etc.) gives about (0.20, -0.60, 0.40) up to sign. Gauss lists +0.21, -0.58, +0.38.
- How the variance 0.68625 itself was obtained (sum of squares divided by which count) is not shown on this page.

Purpose: calibrate the systematic graduation error of the Repsold circle and estimate the accidental reading error of its microscopes.
errors: f(45): recomputation gives (33.45+34.30-71.00+37.35+40.20-76.50)/8 = -2.20/8 = -0.275, not -0.25 as written. The following difference -0.03 is then -0.005 instead. The slip is small and barely affects the harmonic coefficients (alpha changes from -0.747 to -0.745).
f(165) = 8.10/8 = 1.0125 is written as +1.00. The difference column uses about 1.01 (-0.19), so this is only a rounding inconsistency.
Difference at 315: -0.785 - (-0.319) = -0.466. The image looks like -0.48, but the correct value is -0.46/-0.47.

The value sqrt(0.68625) = 0.8284 is arithmetically correct. However, the provenance of 0.68625 cannot be checked from this page.
- Summing the squares of the next page's 36 reading errors gives about 10.07; divided by 20 degrees of freedom (24 equations minus lam, mu, alpha, beta) this would give about 0.50.
- So either a different divisor or count was used, or the residuals differ slightly. This is unresolved.

results.what: Least-squares determination of the non-90deg-periodic graduation error f(x) of a divided circle from readings of three microscopes 90 deg apart, f(x) = (d+a-2b+A+B-2D)/8, with the microscope distances estimated as cycle means
results.modern_name: Least-squares calibration of circle division errors (closure/self-calibration method with multiple microscopes)
results.usually_credited_to: Bessel (Königsberg, from ~1819) for systematic division-error investigations; later Hansen, Wanschaff, Bruns; the general self-calibration principle has many authors

results.what: Fit of the 12 equidistant f-values by a first harmonic -0.75 cos x + 0.36 sin x (coefficients = (1/6) * sum f cos x and (1/6) * sum f sin x)
results.modern_name: Discrete Fourier / harmonic analysis (least-squares trigonometric fit at equidistant points)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange, Clairaut (trigonometric interpolation); Bessel (1815-1828, periodic errors of instruments); Gauss's own interpolation theory (c. 1805)

results.what: Mean error of a single microscope reading from the residuals, sqrt(0.68625) = 0.828''
results.modern_name: Least-squares estimate of standard deviation (mean error) from residuals

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observatory reduction work: calibration of division errors with a least-squares 8-equation scheme, a first-harmonic fit, and a mean error. All the methods are standard and well documented as Gauss's (least squares, mean error, trigonometric interpolation), and Bessel did similar circle investigations at the same time. The page is of interest as instrument history of the Göttingen Repsold circle, not for new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: equals 8*f0, validating the 1/8 formula under the model with sum f = 0
